records.summary: A Figma plugin for browsing and inserting illustrations and other assets, with expanded libraries and commercial team use behind a paid tier. The proposal is a maintained successor to Blush; its current functionality and paid user base are unverified.
records.how_money: Paid tier for expanded libraries and commercial team use; exact proposed price is not stated.
records.customer: Figma users, including teams seeking commercial-use assets.

revenue_claims.claim: Blush had 446,248 reported installs; installs do not establish active or paying users.
A separate tracker reported 666,987 users and 446,845 saves; these are third-party metrics, not verified active or paying users.
Figma reported over 13 million monthly active users in Q1 2025; this is platform audience, not the addressable market for illustration plugins.

records.paid_demand: No lead-specific revenue or paid-user count is verified. Competitor prices are advertised, not proof of sales.

competitors.name: Blush
competitors.price: Current exact price unverified; secondary pages report $12/month billed annually, $15/month billed quarterly, or $20 monthly.
competitors.note: The latest version was reported as published in 2021; current functionality and paying users are unverified.

competitors.name: Illustro
competitors.note: Figma plugin announced June 29, 2026; sells credit packs.

competitors.name: Kitbitz
competitors.note: Announced August 19, 2026 with a Figma plugin and 2,000+ free CC0 illustrations.

competitors.name: GetIllustrations
competitors.price: $195 for one year of illustration access; $249 for one year of Ultimate access with two team seats; or $99 quarterly.
competitors.note: Illustration access plans.

competitors.name: Storyset
competitors.price: Free with attribution; a Flaticon Premium subscription removes attribution.

competitors.name: Icons8 Graphics
competitors.note: Free tier and paid plans; price unverified.

rounds.plain: The ledger says K2 because it found two recent competing or adjacent launches, Illustro and Kitbitz, including free CC0 assets. No lead-specific revenue is verified.

The check found one dated competing launch within six months and did not verify five maintained incumbents meeting its criteria, so it found no kill rule. Later deep evidence identified two recent substitutes, including free assets.

risks: No verified lead-specific revenue, paid users, or recent complaints.
Figma controls plugin review and distribution; plugins must be manually run, and Figma is adding native drawing and vector tools.
The Blush library cannot be redistributed or compiled into a competing service under its license.
Rights clearance, art direction, and quality review require ongoing work.
records.moat: No strong moat is evident. A coherent, independently commissioned or exclusively licensed library and useful team presets could create modest switching costs, but this is not demonstrated.

hours.note: Unverified steady-state target; plausible only with a stable catalog, self-serve billing, and automated routine support.

records.next_steps: First test Blush’s current workflow and paid path. Make a small clickable catalog/team-license mockup and branded page with one proposed price and a refundable preorder; share in a relevant public design community and count only a completed payment from outside the founder’s network.

records.summary: A self-serve monitor that checks a subscription business’s checkout and cancellation flows against DMCC requirements and alerts it to changes needed. Subscription businesses would pay, but the product concept and willingness to pay remain unverified.
records.how_money: Subscription businesses pay; proposed price not specified.
records.customer: Subscription businesses, especially those with consumer checkout and cancellation flows.

revenue_claims.claim: Government estimated 155 million active UK subscriptions and about £26bn in annual consumer spend; these describe the consumer market, not software buyers.
A 2023 impact assessment estimated 236,000 firms (4%) offered in-scope consumer subscriptions; this is an old modeled ceiling, not a current buyer count.

records.paid_demand: No verifiable paid-customer count, sales receipt, or revenue event was found. Subnotice lists zero reviews, which does not establish its users or revenue; competitor prices are asking prices, not realized sales.

competitors.name: Subnotice
competitors.price: Free readiness scans; £15/month for paid features.
competitors.note: Shopify DMCC compliance product; launch reported as 22 June 2026.

competitors.name: Upfront
competitors.note: Adjacent Shopify DMCC audit app; launch reported as 1 September 2026.

competitors.name: DueNotice
competitors.note: Waitlist; launch date unverified.

competitors.name: Evidencee
competitors.note: Terms have placeholder company details; maturity and launch date unverified.

competitors.name: Compliance Radar
competitors.note: Advertises broader law-and-website monitoring; launch date unverified.

rounds.plain: The ledger says K2 because Subnotice and Upfront launched competing DMCC compliance products. It also says the regime is still draft and paid demand is unverified.

The check found the subscription regime remained live and did not evidence a kill threshold. It noted government guidance was expected and no checkout-flow change monitor was found, though later evidence identified adjacent products.

risks: The regulations are draft and applicability depends on the separate commencement of DMCC Act section 254; the stated operative date is unsettled.
The need may be a one-off compliance project rather than ongoing monitoring.
Recent direct or adjacent products are already advertised or launched; their payment evidence is unverified.
Shopify subscription-data access requires restricted scopes and approval; public-page monitoring cannot see all flows.
Legal interpretation and false-positive review need human judgment.
records.moat: Weak at launch: legislation and guidance are public and a basic rules engine is reproducible. Tested mappings to real checkout steps, dated evidence, and customer change history could add retention value, but no exclusive data or meaningful switching cost is demonstrated.

hours.note: Unverified estimate; plausible only for a narrow UK-law public-page monitor with automated crawling and async support.

records.next_steps: Before building, manually create a source-linked sample report for a real public subscription flow and a one-page offer. Test £59/month through a permissioned operator community or opt-in partner channel and require a paid pilot commitment; do not count likes or stated interest.

records.summary: A self-serve checker for landlords’ property portfolios that identifies likely PRS registration fields and missing safety documents. The proposed customer pays for readiness help, though the government already provides free guidance and registration service.
records.how_money: Landlords pay; proposed price not specified.

revenue_claims.claim: England had 5.0 million private-rented dwellings at 31 March 2025; this is a market-size proxy, not the number of in-scope landlords or paying customers.
English Housing Survey counted 4.7 million private-rented households in 2024–25; this is a market-size proxy, not the number of buyers.
NRLA reported 4,000+ landlord sign-ups for its October 2026 database webinar; this indicates interest, not purchase intent.

records.paid_demand: No product-specific revenue or verified paid-user evidence surfaced. Available prices are asking prices, not proof of completed sales.

competitors.name: GOV.UK registration service
competitors.note: Official registration service and readiness guidance; covers the core proposed need.

competitors.name: LetKeeper
competitors.note: Advertises a PRS-readiness spreadsheet.

competitors.name: Letkept
competitors.note: Offers a checker and ledger.

competitors.name: Indate
competitors.note: App includes a per-property readiness checklist.

competitors.name: Lettable
competitors.note: Includes a readiness check.

competitors.name: LetCompliance
competitors.price: Free single-property plan; paid plans from £7.99/month
competitors.note: Advertises a per-property readiness tracker.

competitors.name: Lendlord
competitors.note: Property Register tool reported launched 15 October 2026.

competitors.name: LetProof
competitors.note: Listing describes a property-level PRS checklist; launch date unverified.

rounds.plain: GOV.UK already provides free registration-readiness guidance and the official landlord registration service, including required information and safety details.
The official guidance and registration service cover the core need. Registration is £65 per property annually.

risks: The government service provides its own instructions and support, and the registration task is annual rather than proof of recurring demand.
Several products offer free or bundled readiness checks; a comparable one-off spreadsheet is £4.99.
No product-specific revenue, verified paid users, or willingness-to-pay evidence surfaced.
A standalone checker has weak defensibility; broader local-rule tracking would require ongoing verification.
A full product could involve storing sensitive identity, property, and certificate data.
records.moat: Weak for a checker alone: government publishes the required fields and competitors offer similar checks. A maintained, source-linked rules dataset and accumulated property evidence history could help, but neither is demonstrated.

hours.note: Unverified; plausible only for a narrow self-serve, no-upload product with inbound acquisition.

budget.note: Existing LetKeeper spreadsheet price used as a reference for the proposed demand test, not an established product budget.

records.next_steps: Run a one-day no-code test offering a manually produced readiness pack at £4.99, with a short questionnaire and no document upload or full address collection. Promote through a landlord community with moderator permission or an exact-intent search ad; count payment, not email sign-ups.

records.summary: Complaint intake, evidence, and response tracking software for private landlords preparing for mandatory PRS Landlord Ombudsman membership. The government expects membership in 2028 after the scheme is ready, and the Ombudsman is expected to offer complaint-handling tools and guidance.
records.how_money: Landlords pay; no proposed price is specified.

revenue_claims.claim: England had 5.03 million private-rented dwellings at 31 March 2025; not an exact count of eligible landlord buyers.
HMRC counted 2.88 million UK unincorporated landlords declaring rental income in 2024/25; this is UK-wide and excludes incorporated businesses and some landlords below tax-reporting thresholds.
The Property Ombudsman reported a 58% rise in tenant complaints from Nov 2025–Feb 2026 versus the prior year; this covers agents, not this scheme.

records.paid_demand: No live payment evidence was found for a paid PRS landlord complaint workflow. Dealtwith advertises a pre-launch plan and LetSafe UK offers a £19 template, but neither has sales evidence in the sources.

competitors.name: Dealtwith
competitors.price: Free tier; £6.99/month for up to 2 tenancies, +£2.99/month per extra tenancy
competitors.note: Pre-launch; apps listed as “coming soon”.

competitors.name: Landlord Vision
competitors.price: Starter £19.97/month for four tenancies; higher plans include a tenant service desk and correspondence tracking.
competitors.note: Bundled landlord software.

competitors.name: Landlord Studio
competitors.price: Free up to 3 units; Pro £12/month plus VAT
competitors.note: Established landlord software.

competitors.name: August
competitors.price: Free for up to 2 tenancies; paid price not fetched.
competitors.note: Promotes audit-trail document storage for ombudsman readiness.

competitors.name: LetSafe UK
competitors.note: Complaint response template; sales evidence not found.

rounds.plain: The government expects mandatory membership in 2028 and says the Ombudsman will provide complaint-handling tools. Bundled incumbents and a pre-launch £6.99/month rival cover record-keeping, and no payment evidence was found.
The check found no already-live PRS-specific intake and evidence workflow, and the need had not been delayed beyond 2028. It noted that the Ombudsman was planned to offer tools and guidance.

The trigger is outside the 12-month window, government plans landlord complaint tools, and a near-identical pre-launch offer plus bundled products already cover record-keeping. The sources found no payment for a dedicated workflow.

risks: Mandatory membership is expected in 2028, with no precise start date yet; the trigger is outside the 12-month validation window.
The Ombudsman is expected to offer complaint-handling tools and guidance.
Dealtwith is a near-identical pre-launch rival, while incumbent software bundles related features.
The product would hold tenant personal data and require security and data-protection duties.
Search volume and paid demand for a dedicated workflow are unverified.

hours.note: Unverified estimate for a self-serve log/export tool; customer data duties and rule updates are not measured.

records.next_steps: Recheck when a scheme administrator is designated or a membership start date is published. Then run a one-day concept-page test against the £6.99/month price anchor.
